msg: THE POINT OF THIS BENCH: at R = 52.5 ohm and X = 12.073 ohm the trimmer is PERFECTLY nulled - Im{Zin} measures 1.3e-06 ohm on a 1 A AC probe - and RL is nonetheless exactly 26 dB (rl_b_xcap). The reflection that remains is 100% real and no setting of a shunt capacitor can touch it.

Re{Zin} at that same point = 55.276 ohm. The series 12.073 ohm has been TRANSFORMED into +2.776 ohm of resistance error via Reff = R + X^2/R = 52.5 + 145.75/52.5. That is the mechanism the trimmer cannot fix.
same at R = 50.0 / X = 16.242 ohm: Im{Zin} = 1.6e-06 ohm, a true null.
Re{Zin} = 55.276 ohm - identical to reff_b, because 55.276 ohm IS the 26 dB reflection limit whatever R and X produced it.
closed form: |Gamma| = 10^(-26/20) = 0.050119 -> Reff_cap = 50*(1+|G|)/(1-|G|) = 55.2763 ohm. Matches both simulated probes.
ANSWER TO 'CONFIRM OR CORRECT 12.1 ohm': the network solve reads 26.000 dB at X = xcap_r525_ohm. The closed-form threshold and the simulated one agree to 4 decimal places.
same at R = 50.0: 26.000 dB at X = 16.242 ohm.
X cap at the +5% resistance corner = 12.073 ohm.
the same cap as inductance at 25.0 MHz = 76.86 nH.

CONFIRMS decisions.md / blocks.md s5 ('failure needs X > 12.1 ohm'): simulated 12.073 minus claimed 12.1 = -0.027 ohm, i.e. the architect's figure is correct to 0.2%, very slightly optimistic. Use 12.07 ohm.
CONFIRMS the same claim in nH: 76.86 vs the claimed 77 nH, -0.14 nH.
X cap at nominal resistance = 16.242 ohm (blocks.md s5 says 16.2 - confirmed).
the same cap as inductance = 103.40 nH (blocks.md s5 says 103 - confirmed).

the ceiling the +5% corner starts from: with ZERO reactance and no shunt C at all, Zin = 52.5 ohm exactly and RL = 32.256 dB. Everything the launch inductance does is spent out of this 6.26 dB of headroom, not out of the 26 dB spec.
R = 52.5, X = 11.0 ohm (70.0 nH), perfectly tuned: 26.77 dB - still above spec.
R = 52.5, X = 12.0 ohm: 26.05 dB. Tight bracket (warning severity by design - 0.05 dB is too fine to gate on).

R = 52.5, X = 12.1 ohm - the architect's stated threshold - reads 25.98 dB, i.e. 0.02 dB BELOW spec. With rl_b_x120 this brackets the true cap to 12.0-12.1 ohm and shows the claimed 12.1 is a hair on the wrong side of it.
R = 52.5, X = 12.5 ohm: 25.69 dB - fails, with the trimmer ideal and unlimited.
R = 50.0, X = 15.0 ohm (95.5 nH), perfectly tuned: 27.32 dB.
R = 50.0, X = 16.0 ohm: 26.25 dB. Tight bracket.
R = 50.0, X = 16.35 ohm: 25.89 dB. Brackets the nominal-resistance cap to 16.0-16.35 ohm around the closed-form 16.242.
R = 50.0, X = 17.0 ohm: 25.25 dB - fails even at the nominal resistance and with an ideal trimmer.

IS THE IDEAL TUNER THIS BENCH ASSUMES ORDERABLE? At the +5% corner, yes: the exact null at the 12.073 ohm threshold needs 26.485 pF TOTAL, i.e. 21.785 pF of trimmer on top of the 4.7 pF port - well inside the delivered Johanson 5602's 1-30 pF (parts/5602.json). So the 12.07 ohm / 76.9 nH failure threshold is a property of the topology, not an artefact of an unbuildable tuner.

At R = 50.0 the answer is NO: the null at the 16.242 ohm threshold needs 32.713 pF of trimmer, past the 5602's 30 pF top stop. That is exactly why tuning_authority.cir's exact-null window ends at 94.38 nH (X = 14.825 ohm) while this bench's Reff cap sits at 103.40 nH - at nominal resistance the PART runs out first, at the +5% corner the PHYSICS does.
the same figure as total shunt C: 26.485 pF at the R = 52.5 threshold.
and 37.413 pF at the R = 50.0 threshold.
